metaDescription: Six space heaters with a built-in humidifier compared by mist method, heat type and cleaning needs, so winter air stays warm without drying out your throat.
expertTake: The Dr. Infrared DR-998 is the most complete pick, pairing dual infrared and PTC heating with a humidifier, oscillation and a remote. The Black+Decker model is the value pick, with a humidifier approach that avoids a conventional water tank. Anyone with a large, very dry house should skip the combo idea and run a dedicated humidifier alongside the heater, because a small built-in unit only adds a modest amount of moisture.
introParagraphs: Heating cold air without adding moisture lowers its relative humidity, which is why winter rooms leave throats scratchy and skin tight. A heater with a built-in humidifier tries to solve both problems from one cabinet and one outlet.

The combination comes with real trade-offs. Water and electricity share a body, tanks need cleaning, and the humidifier is smaller than a dedicated one. This guide compares how each model makes its mist, how it heats and how much upkeep it asks for.

products.name: Dr. Infrared DR-998 Dual-Heat Heater with Humidifier, Oscillation and Remote
products.description:
Two heating technologies sit inside the DR-998: an infrared quartz element that warms objects and people directly, and a PTC element that warms the air. The listing claims 60 percent more warmth than a standard 1500W heater, a number that should be read as marketing, but the idea behind it is sound, since radiant heat feels warmer at a given room temperature.

A humidifier, oscillation and a remote complete the package. That makes it the only unit here that attacks dry air, cold spots and operation from a chair at once. The cost is complexity: a heater with a water reservoir and a sweeping head has more parts that can wear or need cleaning.

Fill the tank with clean water and clean it often, since stagnant water breeds mould. Wipe the quartz tubes only when cold. Against the DR-968H below, it adds oscillation and a remote. It suits a large living room where you want warmth and moisture together. Because infrared heat is felt directly on skin and fabric, point the front toward where people sit, and keep curtains, throws and papers well clear of the quartz face. The mist output is best aimed away from the quartz tubes, so give the unit a spot where the water vapour can rise freely and does not drift across the glowing elements.
products.bestFor: Living rooms that need warmth, moisture and wide coverage.
pros: Infrared and PTC elements work together
Remote lets you adjust from a chair
cons: More parts to clean than a plain heater
Marketing claim of extra warmth is hard to verify

products.name: Black+Decker Portable Heater with Humidifier Function and Oscillation
products.description:
The humidifier approach is what stands out on the Black+Decker. The listing contrasts it with traditional built-in water tank humidifying heaters and says this one is different, which is a useful clue for anyone worried about mould in a hidden reservoir. It pairs that with a PTC ceramic element said to take about 3 seconds to heat and a widespread oscillation.

The trade is that a smaller or simpler moisture source adds less humidity than a dedicated unit, so treat it as a mild top-up for a small room. The ceramic heating itself is conventional and fast, suiting a bedroom or an office.

Follow the maker's instructions for filling and wiping the moisture component, and unplug the heater first. Compared with the DR-998, it is simpler and cheaper, and it lacks radiant heat. A known brand with a lighter humidifier is a sensible entry for a small room. Because this design adds less moisture, put a cheap hygrometer on the shelf to see whether the room is actually moving toward 40 percent, and add a dedicated humidifier if the reading stays low. If it does, the Black+Decker is still useful as the heater, and you have not lost anything by buying it.
products.bestFor: Small rooms that want a light humidity boost.
pros: Humidifier avoids a conventional hidden tank
cons: Humidity output is modest for a larger room

products.name: 1500W Dual-Motor Heater with Humidifier, ECO, Manual and Timer Modes

specList.label: Modes
specList.value: ECO, Manual with Fan, Low, High, Timer

products.description:
Two Hi-Velocity brushless motors, a 1500W PTC element and a built-in humidifier make up this small heater, and the listing describes three modes: ECO, a manual mode with fan, low and high settings, and a timer mode. A thermostat sits behind them.

Dual motors are an unusual choice for a small cabinet. The listing does not say what each motor does, so read the manual before assuming that one is devoted to the mist. Brushless motors usually run quieter and last longer than brushed types.

Because the humidifier is built in, filling and cleaning are a regular task. Keep it on a hard, level surface, since water and a tilted body do not mix. Next to the Staholz, it has a plainer look and more explicit modes. Best for a bedroom where you will use the timer. Set the thermostat a degree or two lower than you would for a dry heater, because moist air feels warmer at the same reading, and let the ECO mode taper the output overnight. Avoid placing it near electronics or on a wooden surface that could stain, and give it a trivet if the base sweats.
products.bestFor: Bedrooms that want modes, a timer and moisture from one unit.
cons: Water in the body means regular cleaning

products.name: Staholz 3-in-1 Ceramic Heater with Ultrasonic Humidifier and Ambient Light
products.description:
Ultrasonic mist is the feature to understand on the Staholz. The listing describes an ultrasonic humidifier built into a 3-in-1 heater with cool, low heat and high heat modes, driven by a high-speed 3600 RPM airflow system and an NTC sensor that adjusts the heating output. An ambient light completes the package.

Ultrasonic humidifiers make a fine mist by vibrating water, and they can leave a white film on nearby surfaces if the water is hard. The heater side is conventional PTC ceramic, quick and simple.

Expect to clean the water path regularly, particularly the tank. Switching the humidifier off while the heater runs on high is an easy way to limit damp patches. Beside the Oylus tower, it is a shorter body with a lighting touch. Choose it if you like the mood light. Remember that a humidifier running in a closed bedroom for eight hours can push humidity higher than you intend. A small hygrometer settles the question, and a window that fogs in the morning is the sign to cut back the mist.
products.bestFor: Bedrooms where a soft light and a bit of mist are welcome.
cons: Ultrasonic mist can leave a white film with hard water
Light and extras add parts to clean

products.name: Oylus Tower Heater with Humidifier, Remote, Thermostat and 1-12 Hour Timer
products.description:
The Oylus is the tower of the group, offering low, medium and high heat up to 1500W, a thermostat, a remote and a 1 to 12 hour timer. The listing says the humidifier keeps the room warm without drying it out, in contrast with ordinary heaters.

A tower body gives the mist and the warm air a taller path, which can help them mix. The cost is stability and footprint: a tall unit that holds water should stand on a level, hard floor away from walkways, and a spilled tank is a bigger mess than a fallen plain heater.

The timer is useful because it lets the unit shut off once you are asleep. Clean the tank each week in use and unplug before touching it. Beside the 1500W dual-motor unit, it takes less floor but has less obvious motor design. It is a strong choice for a bedroom corner. Run the first fill with the heater unplugged so you can check for leaks and see how the tank seats, and mark a routine for the weekly wipe on the calendar. A tower that spills is a bigger problem than a box that does, so teach everyone in the house where it stands and keep the cord tidy.
products.bestFor: Bedroom corners that want a tower, a remote and moisture.
pros: Remote, thermostat and 1 to 12 hour timer
cons: A tall body holding water is more of a spill risk

products.name: 70° Oscillating PTC Heater with Humidifier, Remote and 12H Timer
products.description:
A cool-air fan mode, plus 1500W and 750W heat levels, makes this oscillating unit usable all year. The listing claims warmth within 2 seconds from an element with a plate twice the usual area, and lists a remote, a humidifier and a 12 hour timer. Overheat shutoff and tip-over power-off are both mentioned.

The 750W level is the useful one for a humidifier heater: a gentle heat output pairs with moisture better than a full 1500W blast, which tends to evaporate the mist before it reaches the room. Combined with a 70 degree sweep, it spreads whatever you give it.

Plan on the same tank discipline as the others and keep it on a level floor. Beside the Black+Decker, it offers more heat steps and a timer. It suits a small bedroom that you want to use in summer as well.
products.bestFor: Small bedrooms that also want a cool-air fan in summer.
cons: Moisture output is limited by the small tank
Water in the body means regular cleaning

buyingCriteria.explanation: Ultrasonic humidifiers, as on the Staholz, vibrate water into a fine mist and can leave white dust if the water is hard. Others, like the Black+Decker, describe a different approach from a hidden tank. The method decides how much cleaning you do and how much film settles on furniture.

A comfortable indoor humidity sits around 30 to 50 percent. A built-in humidifier adds modest moisture compared with a dedicated unit, so it suits small rooms. If your home sits in the low 20s, plan on a separate humidifier.

Standing water grows mould and bacteria quickly in a warm cabinet. Every model with a tank needs regular emptying and wiping. The Oylus tower and the dual-motor unit both hold water in a tall or compact body. If you will not clean weekly, pick the Black+Decker approach.
The DR-998 pairs infrared quartz with PTC, so it warms objects and air. The others use PTC ceramic only. Radiant heat feels warmer sooner, but ceramic is simpler and cheaper to run.

Full 1500W heat tends to evaporate mist before it humidifies the room. Units with 750W or a low step, like the 70 degree oscillating unit, spread moisture better. Look for modes that let you run humidity without maximum heat.

Never overfill, keep the unit on a level hard floor and unplug it before filling. A tower holding water, like the Oylus, can spill if it falls over. Check that a tip-over cutout is listed and treat it as a requirement.

howWeEvaluated.title: Humidifier design
howWeEvaluated.description: We read how each model produces mist, from ultrasonic on the Staholz to a no-conventional-tank approach on the Black+Decker. We favoured designs that explain the method.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heating quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared infrared plus PTC on the DR-998 against ceramic-only models. Dual-element heating scored higher for living rooms.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning demand
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted tanks and reservoirs because standing water is the main hazard of a combo. Models with less hidden water scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control set
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at remotes, timers and thermostats. The Oylus, DR-998 and the 70 degree unit all include a remote, and the Oylus lists a 1 to 12 hour timer.

howWeEvaluated.title: Realistic moisture
howWeEvaluated.description: We treated every humidity claim as modest compared with a dedicated unit and scored models on how honestly the listing frames it.

cards.label: Ultrasonic
cards.text: The Staholz makes a fine mist by vibration. It is quiet and quick, but hard water can leave a white film. Fresh, clean water and a wiped tank keep it tidy.

cards.label: Other approaches
cards.text: The Black+Decker moves away from a conventional built-in tank, and the DR-998 adds a mist output to infrared heating. Check the manual for the fill and clean routine.

howToChoose.note: Pick ultrasonic for quiet, and a tankless approach if you do not want to clean.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A low heat step that lets moisture linger, a timer, a tank you can clean easily and a level base. Aim for 30 to 50 percent humidity.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The 70 degree oscillating unit pairs a 750W level with moisture, and the Oylus adds a timer. The DR-998 gives the most heat for a bigger room.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The room is large and dry, and you want radiant warmth. The DR-998 covers both with oscillation and a remote.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want a gentle humidity top-up in a small room. The Black+Decker is the simplest route.

maintenance.why: Standing water grows mould in a warm body. Leave the tank open to dry between uses.

maintenance.interval: Every two weeks in hard-water areas
maintenance.why: Mineral deposits reduce mist output and leave a white film. A vinegar wipe usually clears them.
Dust slows the fan and can trigger the overheat shutoff.
A heater near water needs a clean, dry cord. A warm plug is a warning sign.
A damp tank in a closet breeds mould. Dry every part before storing.

faq.q: Does a heater with a humidifier fix dry winter air?
faq.a: It helps in a small room, but the built-in unit is small compared with a dedicated humidifier. In a very dry home you may still need a separate one. Aim for 30 to 50 percent humidity.

faq.q: Are these heaters safe with water inside?
faq.a: They are designed for it, but follow the rules: unplug before filling, never overfill, keep the unit on a level floor and check for a tip-over cutout. Treat water and electricity with respect.

faq.q: How often should I clean the tank?
faq.a: Weekly in regular use, and always before storing. Standing water in a warm cabinet breeds mould quickly. A quick wipe and dry is enough most weeks.

faq.q: Why does my room feel damp near the heater?
faq.a: The mist condenses on cool surfaces when output is high. Lower the humidifier setting or move the unit. Windows with condensation are a sign to cut back.

faq.q: Can I run the humidifier without heat?
faq.a: Some models allow fan-only or a cool-air mode, such as the 70 degree oscillating unit with its cool fan. Check the manual for the humidifier-only option.

faq.q: Which type of mist is best?
faq.a: Ultrasonic is quiet and common, as on the Staholz. Hard water can leave a white film, so clean water helps. A tankless approach like the Black+Decker reduces the cleaning burden.
